messages:
incidents-bot: Paging @eli_oncall — multiple customers reporting intermittent SSE/WebSocket chunk gaps and increased p99 on streaming routes. Alert: streaming.sse.p99 > 1200ms for the last 5m. impact: several keepalive reconnects.
eli_oncall: saw the alert, jumping in. any customer-facing impact yet?
customer-support: getting multiple tickets from 2 customers in EU and us-west. they see long pauses ~10-30s during responses, then resume. no data loss reported, but UX bad.
maya_ops: I'm seeing proxy 504s spike on the streaming gateway around the same time window. also ALB 502/504 traces.
sara_eng: linked traces show message generation is fine on model side — tokens emitted on time — gap appears between gateway -> client. looks like chunk flushes are buffering somewhere.
eli_oncall: hypotheses: 1) proxy write buffer saturation, 2) client slow consumers/backpressure, 3) ALB keepalive/idle timeouts. let's triage quickly.
maya_ops: checking proxy pool metrics: write_queue_depth on sse-proxies jumped to 80% for ~3 nodes at 17:12 UTC. queued bytes spiked.
devops-bot: (automated) Captured proxy pods: proxy-gw-7f6b (node-a), proxy-gw-3a2c (node-c) had TCP retransmits > 5% at 17:12-17:18.
eli_oncall: ok that aligns. sara, can you confirm model -> proxy latency?
sara_eng: model latency steady p95 ~80ms. no corresponding spike. so source is after model emit.
maya_ops: client metrics: lots of long-lived connections, some with tiny recv window growth. suspect slow consumer causing backpressure to proxy write buffers.
eli_oncall: mitigation ideas: increase proxy write buffer flush frequency, temporarily scale proxy replicas, and add a short-term filter to drop connections that exceed Xs of paused output. what do we want first?
sara_eng: quick step: scale proxy pool + add per-connection output buffer limit so slow consumers get errored instead of stalling entire worker.
maya_ops: scaling now: `kubectl scale deployment proxy-gw --replicas=15 -n infra` — from 10 to 15.
eli_oncall: good. also can we bump nginx/ALB keepalive timeout to 60s in the EU LB? current is 15s might be causing premature resets on slow clients.
devops-bot: (automated) Scaling triggered by maya_ops at 17:23 UTC.
customer-support: telling customers we're investigating and may see intermittent pauses; will follow up in 30m.
sara_eng: adding a rate-limiting patch to proxy config: `streaming_write_idle_threshold_ms: 12000` and `max_output_buffer_bytes: 262144` — will roll to one cluster at a time.
maya_ops: rolling config to eu cluster now (canary) — command: ```
kubectl set configmap proxy-config streaming_write_idle_threshold_ms=12000 --context=eu
kubectl rollout restart deployment/proxy-gw -n infra --context=eu
```
eli_oncall: keep me posted on p99 after canary. if it falls then roll global.
(5m later) maya_ops: canary done. eu p99 on streaming routes dropped from 1280ms -> 310ms. write_queue_depth normalized.
customer-support: eu customers reporting much better behavior. us-west still seeing occasional pauses.
sara_eng: next step: push config to us-west, but let's also capture a live tcpdump on one affected proxy to check for retransmits pattern. maya, can you collect /tmp/proxy-dump.pcap from proxy-gw-3a2c?
maya_ops: tcpdump running: `kubectl exec -it proxy-gw-3a2c -n infra -- tcpdump -w /tmp/proxy-dump.pcap port 443`
devops-bot: (automated) pcap stored to s3://redwood-dumps/5370001111/proxy-gw-3a2c.pcap
eli_oncall: good. also let's add a temporary routing rule: route streaming traffic for heavy-tenants -> dedicated proxy pool with larger buffers to isolate noisy tenants. sara, is that quick?
sara_eng: can do via header-based routing in the gateway. adding rule now for tenants: big-corp and streamify. patch: ```
- match: headers["x-tenant-id"] in ["big-corp","streamify"]
  route: proxy-dedicated
```
maya_ops: routing change applied in us-west.
(9m later) maya_ops: us-west p99 decreased from 980ms -> 420ms after routing + config. write_queue_depth still has occasional blips on a couple old nodes.
eli_oncall: any evidence of ALB timeouts still interfering?
maya_ops: ALB logs show idle timeouts matching client pauses at ~15s. I increased ALB idle timeout to 65s for streaming listeners — change in progress.
devops-bot: (automated) ALB config updated at 17:48 UTC.
customer-support: letting impacted customers know we deployed mitigations and will monitor for 1h.
sara_eng: root cause summary so far: spikes caused by a small subset of slow consumers that didn't read from sockets quickly; this causes proxy write buffers to back up and block worker progress, leading to chunk emission pauses to other downstream clients on same worker. ALB idle timeout amplified reconnection behavior for some clients.
eli_oncall: action items: 1) postmortem if recurrence (>3 incidents in 24h). 2) permanent changes: per-connection buffer limits, dedicated routing for noisy tenants, improved telemetry on per-conn stall time, and default ALB keepalive extension for streaming listeners. 3) follow-up: customer outreach and a changelog note.
sara_eng: I'll open a PR with config and telemetry work. tracking tag: SRE-STREAM-142.
maya_ops: I'll rotate the older proxy nodes out and ensure kernel TCP write buffer sizes are tuned.
customer-support: flagged customers for follow-up; created ticket numbers: #C-9123, #C-9124.
eli_oncall: final status: mitigations deployed, user reports improved, monitoring continuing for 1h. unpause escalation if p99 > 800ms again. thanks team :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident note: severity=medium, impacted=multiple customers (not wide), root_cause=client slow consumers + proxy buffer exhaustion + ALB idle timeout. assigned=SRE/infra.
(1h later) eli_oncall: monitoring window clear. closing thread, will file postmortem next week.
_reserved_note: This document is a synthetic Slack thread for dataset generation. All messages are fictional and created for testing purposes.
